s1.syndrome_frame: Painless mass on the frontal bone with a 2-month history and associated radiographic findings
salient_findings: Painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
Soap-bubble appearance on CT of the head
Cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables
key_facts: 50-year-old man
2-month history of a painless mass
Mass located on the right side of the frontal bone
Mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
Mass was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Neurologic examination was unremarkable
Plain radiography showed a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion
CT of the head demonstrated a lytic lesion of the frontal bone
MRI revealed a lobulated frontal-bone mass
Mass was hypointense on T1-weighted images
Mass was hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Mass showed avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Soap-bubble appearance on CT and avid enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with cortical destruction and soft-tissue component

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated mass with fluid-fluid levels on MRI

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass appearance on radiography and well-circumscribed mass

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, radiolucent lesion with avid enhancement

shortlist.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated mass with chondroid matrix on MRI

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with soap-bubble appearance and possible endocrine disorder

raw.rationale: The soap-bubble appearance on CT and the presence of a well-circumscribed, soft, and non-tender mass are characteristic of hemangioma of bone. The MRI findings of a lobulated mass that is hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and shows avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically small, hard, and well-circumscribed, but the described mass is soft and larger than typical osteomas.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are usually located in the epiphyses of long bones and are more common in women, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts often present with pain and swelling, which is not consistent with the patient's painless mass.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia can cause bone lesions, but the described soap-bubble appearance and MRI findings are more characteristic of hemangioma of bone.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastomas are typically smaller and more commonly found in the spine or long bones, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
rejected.why: Chondromyxoid fibromas are rare and usually occur in the metaphyses of long bones, which does not match the patient's frontal bone mass.

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Brown tumors are associated with hyperparathyroidism, but the patient's laboratory studies were unremarkable, making this diagnosis less likely.
